newsitem.title: UK: Laird says 1st 4 months profit up on yr-ago.
newsitem.headline: Laird says 1st 4 months profit up on yr-ago.

text.p: British engineering company Laird Group Plc said on Friday that it had made a good start to the current year with profits in the first four months "a little ahead" of the same period last year.
They said the current performance was achieved "notwithstanding the strength of sterling, higher start-up costs and continuing competitive market conditions," the company said in a statement.
The company told the agm that growth in the current year had been led by its non-auto businesses which produced more than half the group's 1996 profits.

About 70 percent of Laird's profit comes from abroad. "If exchange rates remain at current levels, there will continue to be an adverse impact this year on the translation of Laird's overseas profits to sterling," the company added.
The company says its future depends on its success in expanding into new markets and noted that 60 million stg was invested in 1996 in internal projects and selective acquisitions.

"(The board) remains confident that these investment programmes, together with those planned this year, will provide further opportunities for the continuing growth and development of the group," it added.
